items.title: Teach scenarios lack falsifiable expected outcomes
items.statement: ATS-014 enumerates a very broad set of paths but does not define inputs, expected outputs, pass/fail predicates, fixture identities, or negative oracles for summon disambiguation, model selection, mutation confirmation, memory conflicts, or handoff. Its listed validation surfaces are governance validators rather than executable Teach behavior tests.

items.impact: A test suite could claim coverage while asserting only that surfaces exist.
items.builder_discretion: Fixture organization is discretionary; observable pass and fail predicates are not.

items.title: Teach transition, concurrency, and recovery semantics are absent
items.statement: Save, cancel, conflict, revoke, unlock, mutation confirmation, activity cards, and handoff are named, but legal state transitions, concurrent Teacher-thread behavior, duplicate summons, mutation-versus-cancel races, failed handoff recovery, and rollback semantics are not specified as acceptance oracles.

items.impact: Race-dependent loss, duplicate mutation, or stranded handoff state could pass the stated scope.
items.builder_discretion: Implementation may choose its state machine, but tests need an explicit externally observable transition contract.

items.title: Teach memory lifecycle is only action-enumerated
items.statement: Memory capture actions include scope, revoke, and unlock, yet the core does not establish retention, post-revocation deletion, derived-copy cleanup, export or backup handling, scope-change propagation, or what activity/source disclosure remains after revocation.

items.impact: Revoked or re-scoped Teach memory may remain recoverable or usable without a test failure.
items.builder_discretion: Retention durations may be product-defined elsewhere; the test must still verify the bound contract.

items.title: Teach mutation authority has no actor or approval matrix

dimension_assessments.summary: Future suites are named without executable callers, CI consumers, or failure owners.
Named actions and failure classes lack complete legal-state and transition oracles.
Serialization and idempotency are present, but lifecycle and configuration races remain unspecified.
Provider failure categories and visible fallbacks are addressed, while stateful partial completion and exhaustion behavior are not.
Failed handoff, partial render, notification retry, and import rollback semantics are absent.
Visualizer sandbox and live-send gating are explicit, but Teach mutation actors and stale approval authority are unbound.
No-secret assertions are strong, but retention, revocation, derived data, and deletion are incomplete.
Visualizer parsing and sandbox cases are strong; imported pack and natural-language/source adversarial boundaries are less complete.
Model/source/missing-coverage disclosure, visualizer fallbacks, activity transparency, and non-sound carriers are explicitly required, though detailed oracles remain in other dimensions.
Network retry is named, but offline startup, disconnect, reconnect, stale-state, queue, and cancellation outcomes are not complete.
No systematic corpus, instance, payload, queue, history, quota, or resource ceilings and exhaustion oracles exist.
Accessibility domains are named, but focus, announcement, equivalence, and measurable pass criteria are incomplete.
Localized visualizer feedback is named, while Teach and notification locale, bidi, expansion, and translated-error behavior are absent.
Native adapter and named sound-pack compatibility lack version, atomic migration, rollback, and round-trip oracles.
Activity, receipts, and errors exist, but safe structured diagnostics and correlation across GUI and support evidence are not bound.
Memory revoke and destination delete/update are named without confirmation freshness, undo, atomicity, or recovery outcomes.
Dependencies and owner hints identify seams but do not establish reciprocal integration assertions.
Broad coverage claims lack fixture-bound inputs, expected outputs, failure predicates, and executable gate ownership.
The enumerated cases do not bound emergent combinations, fuzz inputs, schedule perturbations, or provider drift.
